title: Iminodiacetic acid stabilized 3d-4f clusters: Synthesis, structure, and magnetism
claim: Under IDA coordination, Ni(II) and Co(II) hydrolyze on a timescale compatible with lanthanides, whereas Zn(II) and Fe(II) tend to precipitate as hydroxides and do not proceed to high-nuclearity 3d-4f clusters.
explanation: The review ties metal choice to in situ [M(IDA)] stability and matched hydrolysis. Excessive hydrolysis of Zn(II) and Fe(II) is said to stop further interaction with lanthanide ions.
scope: IDA-ligated attempts to make high-nuclearity 3d-4f clusters.
conditions: IDA ligand environment compared for Ni(II), Co(II), Zn(II), and Fe(II).
caveats: The contrast is qualitative; no hydrolysis pH or concentration window is given for the failing metals.
